messages:
mara: quick follow-up from the precision RFC — noticed a long-tail failure on a customer dataset when we flipped to int8 yesterday
aj: saw that in the incident report, any concrete repro?
mara: short repro: prompts with lots of interleaved code + unusual tokens caused hallucinated completions when we used the int8 profile. low-prob tokens drifted up.
vikram: interesting. is this more due to activation quant noise or out-of-range scale shifts?
mara: initial look suggests activation quant noise in early layers cascades. degscore jumps after ~30 tokens.
jules: can you paste the trace snippet?
mara: sure — payload from the canary log: ```
TRACE: request_id=abc123, model=redwood-v1-small, profile=int8-fast, token_idx=34, perplexity_delta=3.8, degscore=0.71
layer_metrics: [{layer:1, rms=0.12, clip_rate=0.001}, {layer:3, rms=0.28, clip_rate=0.04}]
```
sasha: that clip_rate at layer 3 is suspicious for int8. probably needs different scale calibration or per-head scaling.
aj: reminds me of the calibration note in the RFC: per-layer scale + fallback margins. but we never shipped per-head. ops-bot: Canary deploy 1715004000 -> rolled back to fp16 on customer x at 2024-11-02T09:20:45Z :warning:
mara: rollback happened automatically via the degradation policy, which helped customer but we need steady fix.
vikram: two immediate options: 1) tighten the acceptability matrix for canary (lower degscore threshold for int8), 2) implement quick runtime per-request probing and fallback. both have tradeoffs.
jules: runtime probing meaning send a short warmup prompt and compare distributions? that adds latency.
vikram: yes, or a tiny shadow-run: run the int8 path in parallel but don't charge customer until verified. needs more infra.
aj: what about storing sensitivity metadata in quant profiles so runtime can pick safer layers for int8? e.g., mark "sensitive": [2,3] and fall back to fp16 for those layers only (hybrid mode).
sasha: that's promising. hybrid per-layer where we keep critical layers in fp16 and the rest int8. tradeoff: memory and kernel complexity.
mara: also consider "stratified calibration buckets" — we calibrate a profile across slices of prompts: code-heavy, dialogue, math. and have a prompt classifier that picks the right profile.
jules: hmm classifier adds surface area but could be lightweight. we could tag prompts by simple heuristics at ingress.
aj: we should add a short header to requests: `x-precision-hint: code-heavy` so customers can opt-in or we auto-suggest after a few samples.
vikram: we must also improve our offline eval harness: add long-tail probe suite with adversarial token distributions. current eval focuses avg-case.
sasha: +1. include delta-perplexity and per-layer clip-rate, not only end-metrics.
mara: proposed short roadmap: (a) add long-tail probes to eval harness (b) add profile metadata for sensitive layers (c) prototype hybrid per-layer runtime (d) tighten canary degscore thresholds
aj: can we sketch a tiny profile JSON format for (b)?
mara: yep — example: ```
{
  "profile_name": "int8-safe-v2",
  "calibration_slices": ["default", "code-heavy"],
  "sensitive_layers": [2,3,10],
  "fallback_policy": "per-layer-hybrid",
  "confidence_margin": 0.08
}
```
jules: that looks useful. we should version it and add schema checks. also document expected telemetry fields.
vikram: ops question: how do we roll this without huge infra work? can we short-circuit by shipping profile metadata to runtime and using existing mixed-precision kernels?
aj: some infra exists for mixed kernels but control plane needs to pass layer map. that's doable as an MVP: runtime reads sensitive_layers from model config at load time.
sasha: metrics to watch: customer-facing latency percentile, tokens/sec, degscore, hallucination rate (we need a heuristic).
mara: I'll open an RFC follow-up PR with proposed profile schema, eval harness additions, and a small hybrid prototype plan. tagging folks for review.
aj: thanks — happy to help on the schema and telemetry side.
vikram: I'll look at kernel impacts and a perf estimate for hybrid.
jules: I'll add a few adversarial prompts to the probe suite.
sasha: and I'll draft the canary threshold adjustments and an ops playbook for hybrid rollouts.
ops-bot: Note: created issue #QUANT-582: "profile-metadata-and-hybrid-runtime-prototype" assigned to mara.
mara: thanks all. will ping when PR is up. :thumbsup:
